title: GitLab or GitHub: Where Should Your Code Live?
excerpt: Both host Git repositories and run CI/CD, but their strengths differ. GitLab is known for self-hosting and an all-in-one DevOps platform; GitHub is home to the largest open-source community.
verdict: GitLab is the stronger option if you need mature self-hosting or want planning, CI/CD and security in one platform. GitHub is the better choice for working with the open-source world and for its large ecosystem of Actions and integrations.

spec1.label: Self-hosting
spec1.device1Value: Mature self-hosted editions, including a free one
spec1.device2Value: Self-hosting needs GitHub Enterprise Server, which is paid

spec2.label: Built-in CI/CD
spec2.device1Value: Deeply integrated and mature for many years
spec2.device2Value: GitHub Actions is strong and easy to use, though newer

spec3.label: Community and open-source reach
spec3.device2Value: By far the largest home for open-source projects
